fundamental.thesis: ABFRL is India's largest fashion and lifestyle retailer with 1,286 stores across four segments — Pantaloons (value/mass retail, 399 stores, 15.9% EBITDA margin), ethnic brands (672 stores, near-zero 0.1% EBITDA margin), TMRW (D2C digital-first, 75 stores, -19.2% EBITDA margin), and luxury/others (52 stores, 10% EBITDA margin) — competing in an intensely capital-intensive, multi-format environment. Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew a stable +10.6% YoY to ₹2,026 cr with EBITDA margin expanding to 8.2% (vs 5.9% full-year FY26), a genuine operational improvement, but PAT losses deepened to ₹-249 cr (-6.4% worse YoY, -12.3% margin) as TMRW's ₹-42 cr EBITDA drag and ethnic segment's near-zero margins overwhelm Pantaloons' solid contribution; revenue growth has been remarkably steady at 10-11% across periods, but PAT trajectory is deteriorating not improving. P/E is inapplicable given persistent losses; using EV/EBITDA (18.2×, a 22% discount to broad-market peer median 23.3×) and P/Sales (0.92×, below 1 for a consumer brand) valuation appears statistically cheap, but with FY26 FCF of ₹-348 cr, D/E of ~99× (including lease liabilities), and negative interest and debt-service coverage, the discount reflects quality and solvency risk rather than a mispricing — graded fair. The single biggest risk is a prolonged path to PAT profitability: TMRW burns ~₹42 cr EBITDA per quarter with a -19.2% margin (improving by only ₹21 cr YoY), free cash flow is deeply negative, and any revenue deceleration or credit-market tightening could force dilutive equity issuance from a near-52-week-low stock price.

fundamental.thesis: Bata India is India's largest branded footwear retailer (~1,500 stores), competing in mid-to-premium segments where D2C and unorganized competition are intensifying. FY26 revenue was flat at ₹3,530 cr (+0.6% YoY) with H1FY26 decelerating to −2.2%; PAT fell 59.5% to ₹134 cr — partly one-off distorted (FY25 land sale gain of ₹134 cr absent + FY26 VRS/labour costs of ₹49 cr) — but EBITDA margins genuinely compressed from 26.5% (FY25) to 20.9% (FY26), confirming real operating deleverage and not merely a base-effect story. On EV/EBITDA (13.69×, P22 vs broad market, 41% discount to median), the stock screens cheap on operating metrics; however, trailing P/E of 75.6× with ROE of only 8.5% and P/B of 6.43× reflects poor capital productivity — we grade valuation 'fair' using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick per sector card guidance, noting the forward P/E of 37× already prices in a full earnings recovery that ongoing sell-side estimate cuts (−5.8% over 90 days) do not yet support. Three SMP/KMP changes in September 2026 alone raise governance and strategic continuity concerns at precisely the juncture when a clear management reset is most needed.

fundamental.thesis: Blue Star is a leading Indian room air-conditioning (RAC) and electro-mechanical projects (EMP) company, positioned as a mid-tier premium brand competing with Voltas and Daikin in a structurally growing cooling market. In Q1FY27, revenue accelerated to +13.3% YoY (₹3,378 cr) driven by EMP (+15%) and unitary products (+12.7%), but PAT declined 15.1% YoY to ₹103 cr as EBITDA margin contracted sharply from 6.9% to 5.4% — the multi-quarter trajectory shows revenue growth re-accelerating while margins are compressing across all periods (PAT margin: 4.1% H1FY26 → 3.6% 9MFY26 → 4.2% FY26 → 3.0% Q1FY27), a structurally concerning divergence. At a trailing P/E of 62.75× against the Consumer Discretionary/Industrials sector median of ~28–45×, and with BLUESTARCO ranked at P80 in the broad market (78% premium to median P/E of 35.2×) alongside EV/EBITDA of 38.4× at a 65% premium to median, the stock is clearly expensive by both absolute and relative measures — the forward P/E at 40.4× does price in meaningful earnings recovery, but downward estimate revisions of -16.6% over 90 days suggest the market is still re-rating expectations lower. The biggest risk is that cost pressures (crude rising, competitive intensity in RAC) persist through FY27, making the earnings recovery priced into the forward multiple elusive and triggering a de-rating in a premium-multiple name where any guidance miss historically compresses valuation 25–40%.

fundamental.thesis: CarTrade Tech runs India's dominant online used-car marketplace across Consumer (listings), Remarketing (B2B auctions), and Classifieds (auto ads) segments, with a structurally advantaged position as organized channels continue displacing unorganised used-car trade. Q1FY27 revenue grew +16.2% YoY to ₹201 cr — decelerating from the 22–24% corridor sustained across FY26 and the ~37% seen in 9M FY25 — but PAT grew +20.6% to ₹57 cr as EBITDA margins expanded sharply from 32.7% (9M FY25) to 45.5% (Q1FY27), evidencing genuine operating leverage and a cash-backed earnings profile (FY26 CFO/PAT 1.15×). At trailing P/E 58× (P76 vs broad market), EV/EBITDA 41.4× (P83 vs peers), and P/B 5× against an ROE of only 9.8%, the stock is expensive by peer rank; the sector card argues 60–100×+ is achievable for platform models, but the forward P/E of 36.4× shows earnings acceleration is already priced in, and analyst EPS estimates have been revised up +6.8–12% over 90 days, leaving limited further re-rating catalyst. The single biggest risk is further deceleration in top-line growth at a premium multiple — in a RISK_OFF macro with FII selling and rising crude, any Q2FY27 revenue miss or guidance tone-shift could trigger the 25–40% de-rating the sector card explicitly flags for these names.

Chalet Hotels owns and runs upscale hotels in Indian metros, mostly under the Marriott brand, and also earns from office rentals and a residential real-estate business that books revenue in lumps. In Q1FY27, consolidated revenue fell 42.6% YoY to ₹512 cr and PAT fell 57.6% to ₹86 cr (16.8% margin, down from about 22%), but nearly all of that drop came from real-estate revenue collapsing from ₹439 cr to ₹7 cr as project bookings timed out. The ongoing businesses held up: core hospitality grew 8.5% to ₹419 cr at a 29.3% PBIT margin, and rentals grew 18.1%. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA because hotels are capital-intensive. At 15.7x it sits at P27 against the broad market and well below the sector card's premium-hotel range. However, trailing P/E of 26.4x and ROE of 19.1% are flattered by FY26's one-off real-estate profits, so the stock is fair rather than clearly cheap, even near the lower end of its 52-week range (21.8%). Some of the data is unreliable: the 9M and H1FY26 rows look mis-scaled, and the dividend yield is plainly wrong. FY EPS estimates have been cut 2.6% over 90 days, and Q2FY27 results are due soon.

fundamental.thesis: Crompton is one of India's largest fan, pump and small-appliance makers. It leads the market in ceiling fans, reaches about 2.5 lakh retailers, and gained share across most categories between FY23 and FY26 (water heaters +200 bps, residential pumps +180 bps). In Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.8% YoY to ₹2,235 cr and PAT rose about 15% to ₹143 cr (PAT margin 6.4%), up from +7.3% revenue growth in Q3 FY26. But EBITDA margin slipped from about 11% to about 10%, because the company passed on only about 80% of cost inflation despite 10–15% price hikes, and it lost roughly ₹200 cr of primary sales to supply disruption. Trailing P/E is not meaningful because FY26 swung to a ₹-242 cr loss. On the yardsticks I used instead, the stock looks fair to slightly cheap: forward P/E is 23.9x, close to the broad-market median of 23.2x and well below the 60–100x the sector card cites for consumer names, and EV/EBITDA is 20.0x, 14% below the median. However, P/B of 6.0x is above the median, and FY EPS estimates were cut 2.6% over the last 30 days. The biggest caution is that the Q2 FY27 results filed on 2026-10-16 have not been extracted yet, so this view rests on one clean quarter after a loss-making FY26, and several snapshot fields look wrong (113% dividend yield, 5.8 debt/equity for an asset-light business with negative working capital).

Q1FY27 showed a genuine recovery — revenue grew +13.0% YoY to ₹1,458 cr and PAT grew +17.0% YoY to ₹619 cr (42.5% margin), reversing a multi-quarter PAT decline of -5.4%, -13.4%, and -9.4% in the three prior quarters; cricket franchise net revenue (₹630 cr gross, only ₹124 cr net cost) was the swing factor, while core advertising revenue actually fell -2.5% YoY to ₹283 cr, flagging persistent weakness in the traditional TV ad market. At trailing P/E of 12.25× (vs ~35× broad market median) and EV/EBITDA of 4.62× (P2 of 473 peers, -80% vs median 23.3×), SUNTV is unambiguously cheap on every valuation metric — bottom decile on P/E, forward P/E, P/B and EV/EBITDA simultaneously — with forward P/E below trailing (10.7×) suggesting earnings growth is priced in. The biggest risk is structural: linear TV advertising is in secular decline as digital and OTT take share, and sell-side estimate revisions have been negative (-9.8% over 90 days) even as 9 of 11 analysts hold buy ratings — the classic pre-de-rating signal that the recovery thesis may not be as durable as Q1FY27 alone suggests.

Swiggy is India's #2 food-delivery platform (behind ETERNAL) and runs a quick-commerce arm, Instamart, in what the sector card calls the sector's main battleground. That makes it a loss-making business whose growth is still being bought, not a proven earner. In H1 FY27, revenue grew +36.7% to ₹14,383 cr. Q2 alone comes to about ₹7,571 cr (+36%, derived from H1 minus Q1), so growth is steady around 36–37% rather than speeding up; FY26's +51.4% was flattered by the base. The group net loss narrowed from ₹2,289 cr to ₹1,713 cr and the EBITDA margin improved from -15.5% (Q3FY25) to -6.9%. However, the Q2 loss (about ₹922 cr) widened from Q1's ₹791 cr, so the margin improvement stalled in the latest quarter. P/E is meaningless for a pre-profit platform, so I graded it on sales multiple, growth and unit economics, as the sector card directs. At 2.9× price/sales for ~36% growth, near the bottom of its 52-week range (8% of range) and at P37 on P/B versus the broad market, the valuation looks fair, not stretched. The main problem is Instamart: it lost ₹1,415 cr in H1 (-55.9% margin, ~83% of segment losses), so the path to profit depends on quick-commerce economics in a fight for share with Blinkit.

fundamental.thesis: Trident Limited is a vertically integrated home textiles manufacturer (yarn, towels, bedsheets — the dominant revenue share) and paper/chemicals producer, ranking among India's largest terry-towel exporters with domestic paper operations serving as a growing second vertical. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue grew +4.7% YoY to ₹1,787 cr — an acceleration from four prior quarters of flat-to-negative growth — while PAT surged +12.9% YoY to ₹158 cr with EBITDA margins recovering to 17.7%; however, EBITDA itself grew only +1.46% YoY, signalling that PAT outperformance is driven by lower effective tax rates rather than genuine operational leverage, and core home textiles segments (towels −0.06% YoY, bedsheets −2.1% YoY) remain weak. For this capital-intensive textile business, EV/EBITDA of 15.71× (P28 vs broad-market peers) is the primary yardstick and reads cheap, but trailing P/E of 35.09× at the sector median (P50), combined with a low ROE of 8.0% on a 2.84× P/B book and elevated debt/equity, tempers the cheap signal — overall valuation is fair, not compelling. The single biggest risk is the CEO resignation effective September 30, 2026 — the second C-suite departure in two months (CFO also replaced in August 2026) — introducing acute management continuity risk at both top positions while the core business needs strategic direction and EPS estimates have been cut 5% over 90 days.

Urban Company is India's largest online platform for home services such as beauty, cleaning and repairs, and it also sells its own water purifiers and smart locks (Native), runs international operations and has a Saudi joint venture. It is now funding a heavily loss-making quick home-help business called InstaHelp. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹537 cr, up 41% YoY, faster than FY26's +36%. Orders rose 103% and Net Transaction Value (NTV, the total value of services booked) rose 39% to ₹1,432 cr. Profit went the other way: consolidated adjusted EBITDA was -₹144 cr, a -26.8% margin, against +6.8% for FY26. That is because InstaHelp lost ₹174 cr, which wiped out a core business that is profitable and improving (core EBITDA ₹30 cr, up 213% YoY; India consumer margin 3.5%, up 110 bps). Since the business is pre-profit, P/E means nothing here, so I graded valuation on price-to-sales and unit economics instead. At 12.3x sales and 8.6x book value (76th percentile of the broad market), the price is reasonable for 40% growth only if InstaHelp's losses keep shrinking. InstaHelp's loss per order did improve 19% from the previous quarter but is still ₹279. I rate valuation fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is that the InstaHelp cash burn continues while the newly approved ₹2,500 cr capital raise dilutes shareholders, in a risk-off market that punishes high-multiple loss-makers.

The valuation snapshot's trailing P/E of 2.83× is almost certainly corrupted by the June 2026 5:1 bonus split distorting yfinance EPS; using trend-table LTM PAT of ~₹498 cr against ₹29,000 cr market cap implies an estimated trailing P/E of ~58×, well above the 18–28× Auto sector median — graded expensive — and the forward P/E of 38.28× (itself above sector median) confirms earnings are expected to remain well below recent peaks. The key risk is that persistent margin compression and 90-day EPS estimate cuts of 5.8%, combined with a CFO transition in September 2026 and a RISK_OFF macro, leave no near-term catalyst for re-rating toward fundamental value.

fundamental.thesis: Balrampur Chini Mills is one of India's largest integrated sugar companies, with operations spanning sugar milling, ethanol distillation, and power co-generation — a commodity-linked agri-business with meaningful policy exposure (sugar MSP, ethanol blending mandates). The multi-quarter revenue trajectory shows deceleration (from +28.7% in Q2FY26 to +6.1% in Q1FY27), while PAT margins have contracted sharply to 2.7% in Q1FY27 from a prior-year 3.4%, with PAT declining -14.4% YoY to ₹44 cr despite modest revenue growth — this is a deteriorating fundamental picture. At trailing P/E of 38×, BALRAMCHIN trades at the lower bound of the FMCG sector benchmark (40–65×) and sits at P55 in the broad market — the forward P/E of 18.5× (a steep discount to trailing) signals the market is pricing in a meaningful earnings recovery, likely tied to ethanol blending expansion and improved sugar realisations; however, the -20.3% forward P/E discount to peers and P/B of 3.4× (below market median of 4.6×) together suggest fair-to-cheap valuation using EV/EBITDA (25×, slightly above peer median of 23.3×). The primary risk is that this is a sugar company masquerading as FMCG — earnings are seasonal, cyclically volatile, and heavily dependent on government-set cane prices, ethanol blending mandates, and export policy; high debt/equity of 76.6 combined with negative FY26 FCF of -₹349 cr and a suspicious dividend yield of 99% (likely a data artefact) warrants governance scrutiny before any position.

fundamental.thesis: CCL Products is one of the world's largest private-label instant coffee makers, with plants in India and Vietnam (Ngon Coffee, which earned ₹53 cr PAT in Q2 alone), plus a small but growing branded domestic business; it trades as FMCG but is mostly a B2B coffee processor exposed to green-coffee price swings. Revenue growth has slowed sharply, from +44.5% (H1FY26) and +38.5% (Q3FY26) to +13.7% in Q1FY27 and +10.5% for H1FY27 (₹2,411 cr). That implies Q2FY27 grew only about +7–8% (≈₹1,211 cr vs ≈₹1,127 cr), most likely as coffee-price pass-through fades. Profits are still growing much faster than sales: H1 PAT is up 42.5% to ₹247 cr, PAT margin has widened from 8.0% to 10.2%, and cash conversion is strong (H1 CFO/PAT 1.78x, FCF ₹414 cr). Valuation is fair rather than cheap. I used EV/EBITDA because this is a capital- and working-capital-heavy processor, not a classic staples brand: EV/EBITDA is 21.6x (P46 vs market) and trailing P/E is 38.9x, at the bottom of the FMCG 40–60x band but rich for a commodity-linked exporter. Forward P/E of 24.1x already prices in strong earnings growth, and the stock sits at 77% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is that revenue growth keeps slowing toward single digits as coffee prices normalise, while margin gains, which drove most of this year's profit growth, become harder to repeat.

fundamental.thesis: E.I.D. Parry is a diversified agri-conglomerate spanning sugar processing, distillery/ethanol, crop protection (NACL Industries, consolidated Aug 2025), fertilizers via ~60% stake in Coromandel International, and nutraceuticals — functionally a capital-intensive agri-materials holding company where Coromandel's earnings dominate the consolidated P&L, making EV/EBITDA the appropriate valuation yardstick per the sector card's capital-intensive guidance rather than FMCG P/E norms. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue grew just +3.4% YoY to ₹9,018 Cr, decelerating sharply from +29% in Q1FY26 and +25% in Q2FY26 (four-quarter deceleration), while PAT collapsed -42.5% YoY to ₹142 Cr (PAT margin 1.6% vs 2.8% a year ago), driven by PSRIPL refinery closure stripping ~₹911 Cr of sugar revenue, a ₹137.69 Cr PP&E impairment, and distillery revenue contracting -13.5% — continuing a confirmed multi-quarter pattern of decelerating revenue growth AND contracting margins (EBITDA margin peaked at 11.6% in Q2FY26, now 8.7%). On the primary EV/EBITDA yardstick, 5.96× is P2 in the broad market and -74% below median, making the stock technically cheap; however, D/E of 23.65× means interest burden consumes a large share of EBITDA, trailing P/E of 29× exceeds the Materials sector upper bound of 22×, and sell-side EPS estimates have been cut -30% over 90 days, seriously undermining the forward P/E of 10.1× as a genuine recovery signal — overall fair with a value-trap caution. The largest risk is the ₹4,537 Cr provision for aged PSRIPL UAE receivables (RBI FEMA compliance), which if it crystallises as a full loss, further erodes already-stressed book equity and could force deleveraging that impairs Coromandel stake value.

fundamental.thesis: CONCOR is India's dominant rail container logistics PSU (~70% share in rail containerisation), operating EXIM and domestic freight corridors with an embedded structural role in India's trade infrastructure. Revenue growth decelerated to near-zero in Q1FY27 (+0.3% YoY on ₹2,160 cr) continuing a multi-quarter stagnation (Q1FY26: +2.4%, FY25: +2.7%), with PAT essentially flat at +0.1% YoY and EBITDA/PAT margins contracting to 24.5%/12.3% from their 9M FY26 peaks of 26.4%/14.4% — the Domestic segment is structurally weak at a 4.14% PBIT margin and -3.5% volume decline. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive logistics infrastructure business, CONCOR trades at 14.2× — a 39% discount to the broad-market median of 23.3× (P23 percentile), with trailing P/E of 28.5× at the lower bound of the Industrials sector range (28–45×), grading as fair rather than cheap because ROE of 9.8% (below cost of equity) and a very high D/E of 7.39 undermine the P/B multiple case. The single biggest risk is management's bullish FY27 guidance (18% overall growth driven by DFC-JNPA connectivity and assured transit trains) having zero support from Q1 execution, compounded by an unquantified Land License Fee liability with Railways and a governance non-compliance flag (only 1 independent director as of June 2026), both of which create PSU-specific overhang that sell-side estimate cuts (-9.2% in 30 days, -10.5% in 90 days) are beginning to price in.

Using EV/EBITDA as the capital-intensive sector yardstick (per the Industrials sector card), the stock trades at 70× EV/EBITDA and 109× trailing P/E — both at P95 vs the broad market and more than double the Industrials sector benchmark ceiling — at 92.6% of its 52-week high with forward P/E of 51× still well above the 45× sector ceiling, making the stock unambiguously expensive with near-zero margin of safety even after pricing in steep earnings upgrades (+51.7% over 90 days). fundamental.thesis: Data Patterns (India) is a vertically integrated defence electronics manufacturer serving the Indian military and select international customers across radar, electronic warfare, and communication systems — a high-quality niche with exceptional gross margins (78.9% in Q1FY27) and a debt-free balance sheet (net cash ₹466 cr). Revenue grew +16.8% YoY to ₹116 cr in Q1FY27, decelerating sharply from FY26's full-year +31% growth; PAT declined -13.5% YoY to ₹22 cr while EBITDA margins compressed 526 bps YoY to 27.0% — far below management's FY27 guidance range of 35–40% — driven by staff costs surging to 36.7% of sales and the intrinsic Q1 seasonality (Q1 typically ~12% of annual revenue). At a trailing EV/EBITDA of 65.9× against a sector median of 28–45× and a trailing P/E of 99.3× (P93 vs broad-market peers, +182% premium to median), the stock is unambiguously expensive, sits at 97% of its 52-week high, and is priced for near-flawless execution — any disappointment at these multiples historically triggers 30–50% de-ratings in industrial names. The central risk is that margin recovery to the guided 35–40% EBITDA band in H2FY27 is structurally harder given rising employee costs, acquisition integration, and an order book-to-TTM-revenue ratio of only 1.0× offering thin near-term execution visibility.

fundamental.thesis: DCM Shriram is a diversified industrials conglomerate with businesses spanning chloro-vinyl chemicals (caustic soda, PVC), sugar/ethanol, Fenesta uPVC building systems, and agri inputs — holding meaningful market positions in each segment. Q1FY27 headline revenue grew +9.0% YoY to ₹3,564 cr, decelerating from +12.4% in Q1FY26, with operational EBITDA up +12% YoY to ₹364 cr (10.2% margin, expanding); however, reported PAT of ₹693 cr is almost entirely non-recurring — a ₹474 cr favorable income-tax ruling plus ₹79 cr in exceptional asset-sale gains inflate the number, leaving normalized PAT of only ~₹147 cr (4.1% margin), broadly flat YoY on an underlying basis. On the sector-appropriate EV/EBITDA yardstick (the right metric for this capital-intensive, multi-segment business), DCM Shriram trades at 11.86× vs a broad-market peer median of 23.3× (P17 rank — bottom quartile, cheap), and even the forward P/E of 23.3× sits below the Industrials sector lower bound of 28×, making the stock cheap on normalized earnings despite the PAT optical illusion. The biggest risk is that normalized earnings remain structurally modest — agricultural revenue faces an uncertain monsoon (management flags 15–20% sowing area decline) and sugar/ethanol viability hinges on government policy, while elevated leverage (D/E 37.8) amplifies any shortfall in operational cash generation.

Delhivery is one of India's largest tech-led express parcel and freight logistics networks, and its scale grew further with the Spoton merger and the full ₹1,370 cr Ecom Express acquisition (Ecom alone added about ₹1,042 cr of goodwill). In Q1FY27 revenue rose 27.8% YoY to ₹2,931 cr, up from about +16-18% in prior periods, but much of that jump comes from buying Ecom rather than organic demand. Profit moved the other way: EBITDA fell 6.6% YoY to ₹253 cr and PAT fell 65% to ₹32 cr, so PAT margin shrank from about 4.0% to 1.1%, meaning costs are rising faster than pricing. This is a network logistics business, not an order-book company, so I graded it on EV/EBITDA and growth delivery rather than the Industrials order-book yardstick: at 111x EV/EBITDA (P98 vs the broad market), 231x trailing P/E and 41x forward P/E (P84) it is expensive. The 41x forward P/E also assumes a profit recovery that analysts are scaling back, with FY EPS estimates cut 13% over 90 days.

fundamental.thesis: eClerx is a mid-sized Indian data-analytics and process-management outsourcer earning about 78% of its revenue from North America, with 25 clients each paying more than $3M a year. The system tags it Industrials, but its business model is IT/BPM services, so it is graded against IT peers. In Q1 FY27 revenue grew 23.3% YoY to about ₹1,152 cr (only 15.1% in constant currency, so a weak rupee did much of the work) and PAT grew 16.0% to ₹164 cr. Profitability is weakening: PAT margin fell from 17.9% in Q3 FY26 and 17.2% for FY26 to 14.3%, and EBITDA margin dropped from about 28% to 23-24.6% as April wage hikes were absorbed. On valuation it looks cheap: trailing P/E 19.5x is below the 22-30x IT services range, forward P/E is 14.7x, EV/EBITDA is 12.0x (P18 in the broad market), ROE is about 29% and the dividend yield is 3%, with the stock near its 52-week low (10.8% of the range). The biggest worry is cash: operating cash covered just 0.07x PAT in Q1 (EBITDA cash conversion 37.9% vs 75.7% in FY26, receivables at 79 days), and Q2 results land on 2026-10-28, so a second weak-margin or weak-cash quarter could keep the stock falling.

Elecon is a midcap maker of industrial gears and power-transmission equipment (78% of H1 revenue) and material-handling equipment (MHE, 23%), with 22% of sales from overseas and a net-cash balance sheet of about ₹700 cr. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.5% YoY to ₹639 cr and PAT was about ₹97 cr (15.2% margin, about +10% YoY against ₹88 cr). That is better than the 4–6% growth of the previous three quarters, but the 6-period trend still reads as decelerating, and the reported H1 PAT fall of 36.7% is mostly because H1 FY26 included an ₹80 cr one-off gain. On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for capital goods, the stock trades at 20.0×, about 14% below the broad-market median, and its trailing P/E of 40.2× sits inside the 28–45× industrials range, so it grades fair rather than cheap. The order book is up 33% YoY to ₹1,635 cr, but that is still only about 0.7× annual revenue, far less visibility than order-book names usually have, and with next-FY EPS estimates cut 8.1% over 90 days and MHE margins down 540 bps, it is not yet clear that the stock can re-rate.

Emmvee is an integrated solar module and TOPCon cell maker (10.3 GW module and 2.94 GW cell capacity). Its yfinance 'IT' tag is wrong: it behaves like a capital-intensive Industrials/renewables manufacturer, so EV/EBITDA is the right valuation measure. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹3,132 cr (+45.1% YoY) and PAT was ₹762 cr (+79.1% YoY). Growth is clearly slowing from +116% in FY26, while PAT margin rose to 24.3% from 21.4% and EBITDA margin to 35.3% from 34.4%. Q2 module output was up about 40% YoY (952 MW vs 682 MW), but module utilisation is only 44% and Q2 order inflow was a modest 1.5 GW against a 10.4 GW order book. On EV/EBITDA of 13.4x (about 42% below the broad-market median of 23.3x) and trailing P/E of 19.5x (versus the 28–45x Industrials range), the stock looks cheap on paper. That discount is partly fair, though: it reflects peak-cycle module margins, the price sits at 90% of its 52-week range, and next-FY EPS estimates were cut 12.5% in the last 30 days even though 4 of 5 analysts still rate it a buy. The biggest risk is that module margins fall back to normal as domestic capacity floods in, while earnings already convert poorly to cash (CFO/PAT 0.54x).

fundamental.thesis: Engineers India Ltd (EIL) is a government-owned engineering consultancy and EPC company with a dominant position in domestic refinery and petrochemical project services, now expanding internationally (Dangote mega-refinery in Kenya announced Sep 2026). Q1FY27 presents a bifurcated picture: consolidated revenue declined 5.8% YoY to ₹820 cr as the Turnkey Projects segment fell 32.8% (project phasing), but the high-margin Consultancy segment grew 22.9%, driving EBITDA margin to expand sharply to 25.3% from 11.6% prior year, with PAT surging 141.6% to ₹158 cr — though ₹43 cr of that PAT benefit came from a Ramagundam Fertilizers JV recovery that may not fully recur. Using EV/EBITDA (16.75x) as the primary yardstick for a capital-intensive Industrials name per sector card doctrine, EIL trades well below the 28–45x sector P/E median and sits at the P23 cheapest percentile among 473 peers — grading cheap — but the stock is near its 52-week high (86.6% of range) and sell-side EPS estimates have been cut 6–8% over the past 90 days, which compresses the margin of safety. The single biggest risk is the complete absence of disclosed order book or inflow data in Q1FY27 filings: without book-to-bill visibility (the key Industrials KPI), it is impossible to distinguish a temporary execution trough from structural demand erosion in the Turnkey segment, and weak H1FY26 cash conversion (CFO/PAT 0.39x) suggests earnings quality warrants caution.

fundamental.thesis: Siemens Energy India (ENRIN) is a newly-listed (June 2025) power equipment company demerged from Siemens Limited, serving India's electrification build-out across power transmission (55.8% of revenue) and power generation (44.2%) — a structurally well-positioned business but with less than 18 months of standalone track record. Official 9M FY26 filings show revenue of ₹6,791 cr (+31.1% YoY) and PAT of ₹1,128 cr (+52.2%, 16.6% margin) with operating margins expanding 260 bps — a genuinely strong growth print — but three signals undercut the quality: (a) book-to-revenue declining from 2.25× (Q1) to 1.18× (H1), indicating execution outpacing new order wins; (b) Q2 CFO/PAT of just 0.09×, signalling earnings are not converting to cash; and (c) Power Transmission order backlog flat/down (-3.2% YoY) despite the headline growth. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per sector card), ENRIN trades at 70.7× vs an Industrials benchmark of 28–45× implied equivalent — at P95 vs 473 listed peers on EV/EBITDA and P93 on trailing P/E of 102.8× — placing it unambiguously expensive at 90% of its 52-week range with zero valuation cushion. The stock is priced for prolonged flawless execution at peak cycle, and high financial leverage (D/E 4.48×) leaves no balance-sheet buffer if order inflows slow or margins disappoint.

Escorts Kubota is one of India's top tractor makers and also has a smaller construction equipment arm (about 87% of revenue is farm machinery, 13% construction equipment). The sector card's order-book framework is a poor fit for this business, which is closer to an auto or farm-equipment company. In Q1FY27, revenue from continuing operations grew 28.3% YoY to ₹3,208 cr, up from +22.6% in Q2FY26 and -2.9% in Q1FY26. PAT grew only 4.5% to ₹386 cr, so PAT margin fell from 14.8% to 12.0% and EBITDA margin fell 158 bps to 17.5%. Management expects another 1.5-2% of cost pressure in Q2 that price increases will not fully offset. Using the auto/farm-equipment P/E band (18-28x) and EV/EBITDA, valuation is fair: trailing P/E is 22.6x, forward P/E 19.8x and EV/EBITDA 16.3x, about 30% below the broad-market median. The stock is near its 52-week low (7.4% of range), which gives a better entry point but no clear mispricing. The biggest risk is that fast revenue growth keeps failing to turn into profit, made worse by weak cash conversion (CFO/PAT 0.58x in FY26) and Q2 results due on 2 Nov.

fundamental.thesis: Finolex Cables is a leading Indian cables manufacturer with electrical cables (~88% of revenue) and communication/OFC cables (~9%) as core segments, a direct beneficiary of the government-led T&D capex upcycle, 5G rollout, and data-centre-driven optical fiber demand. Q1FY27 revenue re-accelerated sharply to +44.2% YoY (₹2,013 cr) — recovering from a +5.0% trough in Q2FY26 — with PAT up 53.1% YoY to ₹249 cr and PAT margin expanding to 12.4% from 11.2% a year ago; however, the communication segment's exceptional 29.75% margin reflects legacy high-cost inventory drawdown, and management has explicitly guided normalization to low double-digits once that inventory is consumed. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary multiple for capital-intensive industrials (per sector card), FINCABLES at 22.76× sits at the broad-market median (P49 peer rank, -2.4% vs median), while trailing P/E of 24.84× is modestly below the Industrials sector benchmark lower bound of 28×; the stock is at 94.6% of its 52-week range with analyst consensus mean target implying -0.7% from current price, pointing to fair — not cheap — valuation. The central risk is communication cable margin normalization in H2FY27 compressing consolidated margins, compounded by the copper rod plant remaining operationally impaired due to Middle East LPG/PNG supply disruptions.

fundamental.thesis: Firstsource Solutions (FSL) is a mid-cap BPS/digital-services provider servicing Banking, CMT, and Healthcare verticals for global clients, with a growing $1m+ client roster (45 accounts), six consecutive quarters of 4+ large-deal wins, and 11 straight quarters of QoQ revenue growth — the deal pipeline signals reasonable near-term revenue visibility for its scale. Q1FY27 delivered 12.3% constant-currency revenue growth — a sharp deceleration from +24.5% a year ago — while adjusted PAT grew +31.2% YoY to ₹22cr (8.2% margin) and EBIT margin hit 12.4% for a seventh consecutive quarter of expansion; the company maintained FY27 guidance of 10-13% CC growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin despite absorbing a 1-1.5% headwind from a healthcare BPaaS wind-down, a show of confidence in the deal ramp pipeline. On valuation, trailing P/E of 25.1× sits within the IT sector benchmark of 22-30×, but EV/EBITDA of 12.5× ranks at the P20 percentile of the broad market (-47% below the market median of 23.3×) and forward P/E of 15.25× trades at a -34% discount to the market median — with the stock at 18.8% of its 52-week range, the risk/reward skews cheap, though in a RISK_OFF, FII-selling environment the re-rating catalyst is absent near-term. The dominant risk is that CC revenue growth has halved over four quarters, the 27.5% voluntary attrition rate constrains margin expansion headroom, and a 66% concentration in cyclical Banking+CMT verticals leaves earnings vulnerable to any corporate IT/BPS budget tightening.

Gallantt Ispat is a mid-sized integrated long-steel maker (TMT bars and billets, plus captive power). The desk tags it Industrials, but the business is really Materials and has no order book. H1 FY27 revenue rose 6.7% YoY to ₹2,292 cr, but PAT fell 29.9% to ₹184 cr and the PAT margin compressed from about 12.2% to 8.0%. Subtracting Q1 from H1 gives an implied Q2 of about ₹1,146 cr revenue (roughly +12% YoY) and only about ₹60 cr PAT (roughly -32% YoY, a 5.2% margin), so profitability is getting worse even as volumes recover. Cash conversion also weakened: H1 CFO/PAT was 0.49x and FCF was -₹188 cr, as ₹278 cr of capex outran ₹91 cr of operating cash, compared with 1.24x and +₹254 cr FCF in FY26. On valuation, the trailing P/E of 36.9x and P/B of 5.4x look expensive against the 12–22x Materials norm for a cyclical steel business. EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick here, was not available, and the broad-market peer fallback calls it 'fair' only because no tight steel peers are in the universe. The biggest risk is further margin compression from steel price weakness and rising crude/input costs while capex keeps free cash flow negative.

fundamental.thesis: Great Eastern Shipping is India's largest private shipping company operating tankers and offshore OSVs, currently leveraged to elevated global tanker charter rates driven by the crude upcycle. Q1FY27 revenue surged +66.9% YoY to ₹2,005 cr with PAT jumping +159.3% to ₹1,309 cr — a sharp V-shaped reversal from four prior quarters of accelerating decline (peak drawdown -20.3% in Q1FY26) — with PAT margins expanding from 37.8% to 57.2% and EBITDA margins hitting 70.8%, powered by the shipping segment's 90.2% YoY growth and aggressive debt reduction (total debt ₹799 cr vs ₹1,853 cr a year ago, net cash ₹3,009 cr). At EV/EBITDA of 4.69× (primary yardstick for capital-intensive shipping) and trailing P/E of 6.86×, GESHIP ranks at P3 among 473 market peers — unambiguously cheap in absolute terms, though shipping's structural cyclicality anchors multiples at depressed levels and the forward P/E (7.17×) marginally exceeding trailing (6.86×) signals expected deceleration. The primary risk is that Q1FY27 earnings represent a cyclical peak: ₹124.84 cr of non-recurring vessel-disposal gains inflated PAT, charter rates are historically mean-reverting, and the RISK_OFF macro with FII selling (-₹41,850 cr 30-day net) adds near-term multiple-compression pressure on a mid-cap name.

fundamental.thesis: GMR Airports is India's largest private airport infrastructure conglomerate, operating Delhi, Hyderabad, and a fast-expanding portfolio including newly commissioned Nagpur and Bhogapuram airports — giving it direct, long-duration exposure to India's structural aviation growth story but also a highly leveraged balance sheet with ~₹938 cr/quarter in interest charges. Q1FY27 revenue grew +23.0% YoY to ₹4,085 cr, a marked deceleration from the +48.6% peak in Q3FY26, while PAT recovered to ₹148 cr (vs -₹137 cr in Q1FY26), but EBITDA margins have contracted from 43.8% to 38.4% over the same window — partly driven by Hyderabad traffic declining 12.1% YoY and Mopa international traffic collapsing 43% on West Asian geopolitical disruption. Valuation must use EV/EBITDA — P/E of 850× is meaningless on thin margins and negative book value is a structural artefact of leverage — at 25.1× EV/EBITDA vs a broad peer median of 23.3× (P56 rank), the stock is fairly priced at best, yet it sits at 98.1% of its 52-week range with near-term EPS estimates cut -8.8% in 30 days, leaving an asymmetric risk/reward. The biggest risk is that the traffic-driven EBITDA compression at flagship Hyderabad (a direct revenue driver, not a lagging indicator) deepens faster than new airport ramp-ups at Nagpur and Bhogapuram can offset it, given the high fixed-cost and debt-service burden.

fundamental.thesis: Godrej Industries is a diversified conglomerate holding company with operating stakes across chemicals (Godrej Agrovet/Astec), real estate (Godrej Properties), finance (Godrej Capital), dairy (Creamline), and crop care — a structure that typically warrants a holdco discount to sum-of-parts. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue accelerated to +22.2% YoY (₹5,448 cr), but PAT to owners collapsed 36.5% YoY to ₹239 cr, with PAT margin contracting sharply to 4.4% from 7.8% a year ago — a dangerous divergence driven by rising interest costs (D/E worsened to 2.38x from 1.90x), a loss-making dairy segment, and a -17.5% YoY revenue decline in the high-margin real estate segment. fundamental.thesis: Clean Science and Technology is a specialty chemicals manufacturer with a proprietary catalytic-process moat, producing high-margin performance chemicals (MEHQ, BHA, Anisole) that historically command EBITDA margins above 40% — well above commodity Materials peers. Revenue growth has deteriorated sharply: from +8.4% YoY in Q1FY26 through a brief +16.1% phase, then crashing to -2.2% YoY in H1FY26, while PAT margins have contracted sequentially from 28.8% to 25.9% over the same window — a consistent multi-period compression signal, not a one-off. Using EV/EBITDA (24.4×) as the primary yardstick for capital-intensive specialty chemicals (per sector card), the stock sits at P56 versus broad market peers — fairly valued — with trailing P/E at 38.77× well above the 12–22× Materials sector benchmark, partially justified by franchise-quality margins; however, 90-day sell-side EPS revisions of -4.5% directly undermine the steep earnings recovery that the 26× forward P/E implies. The biggest risk is that the combination of negative revenue growth (-2.2%), contracting PAT margins, and extremely weak cash conversion (CFO/PAT of only 0.32× in HY FY26) could derate this premium multiple materially if the Q2FY27 results confirm operational deterioration rather than a cyclical bottom.

fundamental.thesis: Dalmia Bharat is India's fourth-largest cement producer by capacity (~55 MnTPA post-Jaypee acquisition), with a concentrated east/south India franchise competing in a consolidating industry where UltraTech+Adani control ~45% capacity, conferring moderate but not dominant pricing power. Revenue growth moderated from +10.7%/+10.2% in Q2/Q3 FY26 to +7.0% YoY in Q1FY27 (₹3,890 cr), while PAT collapsed 52.2% YoY to ₹188 cr (4.8% margin vs 10.9% in Q1FY26) — partly from ₹182 cr exceptional acquisition charges, but more structurally, EBITDA/tonne has deteriorated from ₹1,261 in Q1FY26 to ₹823 in Q3FY26, meaningfully below the ₹900–1,100 healthy range for Indian cement, flagging genuine pricing and cost pressure beyond the one-offs. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for capital-intensive cement (sector card guidance), at 12.26× vs a broad-market median of 23.3×, DALBHARAT ranks P19 cheapest vs peers and grades fair — the trailing P/E of 35× overstates expensiveness due to exceptional-charge distortion, and the forward P/E of 23.94× is more representative of the recovery trajectory, though high post-acquisition leverage (D/E flagged HIGH, finance costs ₹147 cr in Q1FY27) constrains the upside re-rating case. The near-term risk is management-guided input cost inflation of ₹70–80/tonne in Q2 FY27 extending PAT compression before Jaypee's 5.2 MnTPA capacity contributes meaningfully from Q3 FY27, with the Bawri Group DCNEL arbitration adding unquantified litigation tail risk.

Deepak Fertilisers is a mid-cap ammonia-chain business. It makes industrial chemicals (nitric acid, IPA, methanol), it is a leading Indian producer of technical ammonium nitrate (TAN) for mining, and it sells crop nutrition (NPK, specialty fertilisers), with large new capacity at Gopalpur (TAN) and Dahej (nitric acid) due to start in Q2 FY27. On the official filings, FY26 revenue grew 12.0% to ₹11,506 cr, but PAT fell 21.8% to ₹739 cr. Profitability has been shrinking through the year: PAT margin slid from 8.1% (H1) to 7.0% (9M) to 6.4% (full year), and EBITDA margin from 17.3% to 14.6%. The filing-extracted trend table has no Q1 FY27 revenue or PAT, and the unverified yfinance figure (PAT ₹490 cr on ₹1,886 cr revenue) looks like it may include a one-off. Treating this as a cyclical chemicals business, we judge it on EV/EBITDA: 11.1× is about half the broad-market median (bottom 15% of the market), but it is above the 5–8× the sector card calls normal for chemical cyclicals at mid-cycle. Trailing P/E of 16.9× sits inside the 12–22× Materials range, so overall we grade it fair. The forward P/E of 10.6× and analysts raising this year's earnings estimates by 43% over 30 days already assume the new plants succeed. The biggest risks are a slow ramp-up at the new plants with debt high (debt/equity about 0.76) and free cash flow negative (−₹396 cr in H1 FY26), together with raw-material squeeze from the Middle East and a falling-margin trend.

fundamental.thesis: FACT is a PSU fertilizer producer (primarily complex fertilizers under the FACTAMFOS brand) operating as a near-monopoly in Kerala/South India, heavily dependent on government subsidy disbursements and imported raw materials — a price-taker in both inputs and outputs. Revenue recovered sharply to ₹1,484 cr in Q1 FY27 (+41.9% YoY, accelerating from the -24.9% trough of 9M FY2025), but this top-line bounce has not translated into operating profits: the fertilizer segment PBIT margin sits at -1.86%, the Q1 FY27 operating loss before finance costs was ₹36.51 cr, and the headline PAT of ₹3 cr (0.21% margin) is a statistical artefact of non-operating income rather than genuine operational recovery — full-year FY26 PAT was -₹40 cr. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per the sector card), FACT trades at 120.63× vs a fertilizer/chemicals cyclical mid-cycle norm of 5–8×, ranks P99 among 403 broad-market peers, and carries a P/B of 36.81× on a near-zero ROE — this is unambiguously expensive; the ₹50,886 cr market cap is disconnected from any demonstrated earnings power. The single largest risk is the compounding of a post-Q1 raw-material supply shock (West Asia geopolitical disruptions already causing plant shutdowns) on top of extreme financial leverage (D/E 295×) where quarterly finance costs of ₹61.98 cr structurally exceed operating income, leaving zero buffer for further stress.

fundamental.thesis: Gujarat Fluorochemicals is India's dominant integrated fluorochemical and fluoropolymer producer — holding a near-monopoly in domestic ref-gas (R32, R134A) and fluoropolymers — now executing a high-stakes diversification into EV battery materials via its GFCL EV subsidiary. Q1FY27 revenue of ₹1,588 cr grew +24% YoY with EBITDA expanding 24% to ₹428 cr (27% margin) and PAT +20% YoY to ₹219 cr (14% margin), representing a sharp re-acceleration from the -1.1% revenue trough in Q3FY26, driven by a fluorochemicals surge of +52% YoY; the PAT margin trajectory remains mixed however — recovering from Q4FY26's 8.2% trough but still below the 14.6% achieved in H1FY26, and the trajectory signal flags structural compression as the loss-making battery materials drag deepens (GFCL EV EBITDA -144% on ₹14 cr revenue in Q1FY27). Valuation is unambiguously expensive using EV/EBITDA — the primary yardstick for capital-intensive specialty chemicals — at 42.17×, a level that far exceeds even premium Indian specialty chemical peers trading at 20–30×, and is well above the 5–8× mid-cycle benchmark for commodity chemicals; the stock sits at 91.5% of its 52-week range and consensus estimate revisions are running -5.4% on a 90-day basis, a classic pre-derating signal. The central risk is execution on a ₹6,000 cr capex commitment by FY28 for a segment (battery materials) that posted a ₹30 cr EBITDA loss on ₹14 cr revenue in the latest quarter, compounding an already negative FY26 FCF of ₹-291 cr and high reported leverage.

fundamental.thesis: GMDCLTD is a Gujarat state-government PSU primarily engaged in lignite mining (92% of segment revenue) with a structurally loss-making power segment; it is a commodity cyclical where EV/EBITDA — not P/E — is the correct yardstick per the sector card. Q1FY27 showed a revenue recovery to ₹907 cr (+23.8% YoY) driven by mining (+22.7% to ₹841 cr), but PAT was essentially flat at ₹163 cr (-0.2% YoY), with PAT margin compressing sharply from FY26's elevated 36% to 18% — operating leverage destroyed by a 13-fold surge in finance costs (₹6.61 cr vs ₹0.51 cr YoY) and the power segment swinging to a ₹6 cr operating loss from a ₹10.6 cr profit. At EV/EBITDA of 43.9× (P85 vs 473 broad-market peers, +88% premium to the median 23.3×), the stock is expensive on its primary capital-intensive multiple despite a superficially cheap trailing P/E of 20.6× (P23) — the P/E is optically cheap because ₹324 cr in FY26 non-operating interest/dividend income inflates PAT well above operating earnings, a persistent distortion for this PSU. The biggest risk is the structural squeeze: negative FCF (−₹290 cr FY26), a capex/revenue ratio of 39%, rapidly rising debt-servicing costs, and a power segment with a −36.9% operating margin in FY26 that shows no credible path to profitability.

fundamental.thesis: Gravita India is India's leading integrated metal recycler (lead, aluminum, copper, plastics), operating across 11 countries and recently consolidated to 99.57% ownership of Rashtriya Metal Industries Limited (RMIL) in the copper segment. Q1FY27 revenue surged +43.1% YoY to ₹1,475 cr, but this is materially inorganic (RMIL-driven copper volumes); PAT grew only +14.3% YoY to ₹106 cr as EBITDA margin contracted to 10.7% from a 12.4% peak in 9M FY26 — the copper segment's dilutive ~4% EBITDA margin versus 10–13% for core legacy segments is compressing group-level profitability, and FCF was -₹49 cr in FY26 with CFO/PAT of only 0.44×, flagging weak earnings quality. At a trailing P/E of 33.15× and EV/EBITDA of 23.98×, GRAVITA trades well above the Materials sector benchmark (P/E upper bound ~22×; cyclical EV/EBITDA norms 5–8×); the forward P/E of 21.67× implies the market is pricing in sharp earnings recovery, but against contracting margins and negative FCF this premium looks stretched — we grade valuation expensive. The primary risk is that RMIL integration structurally lowers group EBITDA margins for 2–3 more quarters while high leverage (D/E flagged at ~30×) and a ₹70.1 cr customs demand under appeal create balance-sheet and regulatory overhang in an already risk-off macro environment.

fundamental.thesis: Hindustan Copper (HINDCOPPER) is India's only vertically integrated copper mining and smelting PSU, with a near-monopoly on domestic copper ore mining and implicit government backing as a strategic-metal producer. Q1FY27 delivered revenue of ₹936cr (+81.4% YoY) and PAT of ₹352cr (+162.5% YoY), with PAT margin expanding sharply to 37.6% from 26.0% a year ago and EBITDA margin surging to 56%; growth has clearly accelerated from a muted +4.6% YoY in Q1FY26, driven overwhelmingly by higher copper realisations rather than volume — a commodity-price-lift story, not a structural earnings re-rating. Using EV/EBITDA as the correct yardstick for a capital-intensive commodity cyclical (per sector card), HINDCOPPER trades at 33.4× — more than 4× the mid-cycle cyclical benchmark of 5–8× and +43% above the broad-market median (P70); trailing P/E of 53.5× is also far above the Materials sector range of 12–22×, grading the stock as expensive. The critical risk is that copper-price cyclicality combined with high financial leverage (D/E 3.32), negative FY26 FCF (-₹182cr), a thin analyst base (1 analyst), and the absence of management guidance creates severe downside asymmetry if LME copper prices correct or China demand weakens — macro headwinds (risk-off, rising crude, weakening INR) compound this.

fundamental.thesis: Hindustan Zinc is India's dominant integrated zinc-lead-silver miner (Vedanta Group subsidiary) with near-monopoly status in domestic mined zinc and structural cost advantages that produce world-class EBITDA margins of 62.4% — a level no domestic peer can match. H1FY27 revenue surged 76.7% YoY to ₹28,840 cr (accelerating sharply from -4.4% in Q1FY26), PAT grew 143.4% YoY to ₹11,881 cr, and PAT margin expanded to 41.2% from 29.9% — a five-period trajectory of simultaneously accelerating revenue growth and expanding margins driven primarily by elevated zinc and silver commodity prices, with cash quality strong (CFO/PAT 1.12×). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive commodity miner, the stock trades at 10.59× — P13 among 473 peers and a 54.6% discount to the broad-market EV/EBITDA median — with trailing P/E of 17.46× squarely inside the Materials sector range (12–22×), grading cheap on peer-relative metrics, though 10.59× sits above the 5–8× typical mid-cycle range for base-metals cyclicals, signalling that some commodity-cycle-peak risk remains unpriced. The thesis is materially constrained by an unresolved ED/FEMA investigation (search and seizure June 2026, no regulatory communication as of the October 2026 filing) and SEBI observations on related party transaction disclosures — governance headwinds typical of Vedanta Group that can trigger a de-rating independent of commodity fundamentals, and are weighted heavily under the midcap governance overlay.

Himadri Speciality Chemical is a mid-cap specialty chemicals maker built around carbon black and coal-tar derivatives. It is expanding into battery anode material, adding 70,000 MTPA of speciality carbon black in Feb 2026 and 200 MTPA of anode capacity in Apr 2026, and it is taking over Dalmia Bharat Refractories' tyre business from 1 Oct 2026. In H1FY27, revenue jumped 42.8% YoY to ₹3,123 cr, a sharp pick-up from +1.0% in FY26 and -6.3% in H1FY26. fundamental.thesis: National Aluminium Co. (NALCO) is India's largest integrated aluminium producer — bauxite mining through primary metal smelting with captive power — and a global low-cost leader in alumina, giving it structural cost advantages over most non-Chinese peers. Q1FY27 revenue surged +39.3% YoY to ₹5,302 cr while PAT jumped +88.2% YoY to ₹2,002 cr with EBITDA margin expanding to 54.3%, driven by the aluminium segment (+89.6%) on higher LME realisations ($3,154/tonne); however, volume growth is absent — domestic metal sales fell 1.32% YoY, alumina production was flat at 0% growth, and the Pottangi bauxite mine expansion is stalled due to local agitation. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive cyclical (sector card guidance), NALCO trades at 7.4× — at the lower bound of the 5–8× mid-cycle range for commodity materials and at the P5 peer percentile among 473 NSE-listed stocks, flagging genuine cheapness in absolute and relative terms, though peak-earnings caution applies since low multiples on cyclicals often reflect LME normalisation risk. The single biggest threat is LME aluminium price mean-reversion: earnings are entirely price-led rather than volume-led, so a 15–20% LME retreat would substantially compress EBITDA margins and unwind the cheap valuation signal.

books.title: Fundamental grades → rules
books.hypothesis: Strong growers that are not yet decelerating, held whole and long: the one filter with measured forward information (+2.5 pp at 60 sessions, +5.6 pp at 120 vs the equal-weight universe in the point-in-time study), alone — kept at target weight and re-qualified every 120 sessions.

rules.eligible: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes)
rules.rank: revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth == strong, risk != high, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (growth not strong, risk high or decelerating); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session

rules.universe: close > own 200-day SMA, 12-1 momentum known AND the shared fundamental filter (growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes))

books.title: Technical pullback in uptrends
books.hypothesis: Technicals the right way round in a mean-reverting tape: buy the dip in a leader and give it time — a 10-session minimum hold and a 20-session cap keep the edge from being traded away in charges.
